sections.label: Bill clauses amending health legislation
sections.summary: Clauses 2, 5, 8, 17, 19, 20, 23, 25 and 27 amend nine named health-related Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clauses 2, 5, 8, 17, 19, 20, 23, 25 and 27 of the Bill amend various legislation, namely, the Allied Health Professions Act 2011, the Dental Registration Act 1999, the Health Products Act 2007, the Medical Registration Act 1997, the Nurses and Midwives Act 1999, the Optometrists and Opticians Act 2007, the Pharmacists Registration Act 2007, the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act 1993 (or TCASA), and the Traditional Chinese Medicine Practitioners Act 2000.

sections.label: Penalties channelled to Consolidated Fund
sections.summary: Clauses 8, 19 and 23 amend three Acts to channel penalties and composition sums into the Consolidated Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clauses 8, 19 and 23 of the Bill amend section 65(3) of the Health Products Act 2007, sections 42 and 43A of the Nurses and Midwives Act 1999, and sections 63 and 69(4) of the Pharmacists Registration Act 2007 to channel penalties and composition sums collected under those Acts into the Consolidated Fund.

sections.label: Deletion of superseded provisions and Development Fund
sections.summary: Superseded provisions will be deleted, and clause 6 requires Contingencies Fund advances to the Development Fund be authorised by warrant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These provisions have since been superseded by subsequent amendments, revisions or repeals, and for good order, these provisions will be deleted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: I now come to clause 6, which amends section 6 of the Development Fund Act to require that advances from the Contingencies Fund for the Development Fund must be authorised by a warrant issued under the authority of the Minister for Finance.

sections.label: Maintenance of Parents Act amendments
sections.summary: Clause 15 clarifies 2023 amendments by removing the age limitation for a child and addressing claims and Tribunal powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Moving on, clause 15 amends the Maintenance of Parents Act 1995 to clarify two amendments that were made through the Maintenance of Parents (Amendment) Act 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It removes the age limitation in the definition of "child" in section 2 and inserts a new section 3AA to clarify that no claims or applications for maintenance can be made against a child below 21 years of age at the point of the claim or application and it inserts new subsections 2A and 2B in section 8 to clarify the Tribunal's powers to give directions and make orders when hearing variation or rescission applications.

sections.label: Medical Registration, law enforcement, Town Councils amendments
sections.summary: Clause 17 allows extensions of time, clause 21 amends law enforcement definitions, and clause 26 inserts a vehicle reference.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 17 amends section 59A(11)(a) and section 59U(1) of the Medical Registration Act 1997 to allow applications for extension of time of up to nine months per extension to be granted for matters before the Disciplinary Tribunal, Complaints Committee or Review Committee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Both provisions also confer discretion to grant longer extensions of time exceeding nine months where there are circumstances beyond the control of the respective tribunal or committee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The next clause, clause 21 makes three amendments: first, it amends the definition of "law enforcement agency" to include any department or office of a public body that is similar to the departments or offices in paragraphs (a) to (d) of that definition, prescribed by the Minister for Home Affairs by notification in the Gazette; second, it amends the definition of "law enforcement officer" to include any officer or class of officers of a public body authorised in writing by the Minister; and third, it introduces a definition for "public body" to mean a body corporate established by a public Act for the purposes of a public function but excludes Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Next, clause 26 amends section 82(2) of the Town Councils Act 1988 by inserting a reference to "vehicle" to make it clear that the Minister for National Development has the power to prescribe model by-laws that confer power on Town Councils for the storage and disposal of goods left on common property and that extend to vehicles such as bicycles and personal mobility devices.
